I'll start by saying police+criminal justice, army, and fire services should be in the hands of the government. I want to be able to travel the country and not be arrested by some random person's security team. Sure, hire security teams, but the power to arrest and detain/jail shouldn't be in the hands on any random person that has a team of armed guards.

Army / national security is a no brainer imho... This army is going to go fight for freedom of just some of the people in this country? We'll defend your house from foreign invaders but not your next door neighbors?

Fire is I think also a public good. I don't want my house to catch on fire if my neighbors is on fire and they're not paying so they wait until mine is on fire. Also things like forest fires, etc where it's no ones property but pose a danger to everyone around it if it's not checked.

Any other services that you can think of that should be in government hands?
What areas do you think the government needs to be providing through taxes versus privatizing it?
Basic education should probably be free and provided for as well. That would most likely mean that the government should provide it from the taxes we pay. It shouldn't be compulsory though.

Police: If we are talking about pure policing for the safety from people who would break the NAP and try to infringe on your rights, then I am fine with public or private. I am not ok with Law Enforcement or Thugs of the state. Just because someone passes a law 1000 miles away from me with out my consent, does not mean I need to follow that law unless it up holds the NAP and property rights.

Military: Protection of the homeland is important. That said in a country like the US, we are a bit over blown on this. Our country is boarded by our Allies, and we have two huge oceans separating us most other nations. Having a homeland defense force is a great idea, but an offensive military used to force our will on other countries is immoral and crazy. I think that having citizens trained to defend their homeland makes sense, but a standing army is just a huge waste of money.

Fire protection: Many fire departments in our country are volunteer fire departments. I would posit that volunteer fire departments are just as good as their paid counter parts. Having this cuts down on the cost, and increases community involvement. Also as it goes for forest fires, they are a good thing, and necessary in nature. Our current preventative measures have unintended consequences of creating larger and less controllable fires. Allowing forest fires to burn is a good thing. If your house is in the middle of the woods, and you dont have the recommended buffer area around your house, then that is your problem and not societies...

What should the government provide through theft you ask? Nothing. Everything should be voluntary, if you don't think that a government service is good, then you should not have to pay for it. Taxation creates a crazy upside down world, where failed results drive more money to that service. In capitalism we have the exact opposite, success breeds more money not failure.

Infrastructure, Emergency/Law Enforcement Services and Military. I also have no real objection to some form of governmental welfare/healthcare, however, I think it needs to be more tightly controlled.

Personally I think there should be a divide between needs and wants. Everyone pooling together to reduce the cost of needs as much as we can. Normally I'd say it doesn't matter much if it's private or public, but we are getting into a sweet spot with technology where we can either lower costs to increase private profits or lower costs to save everyone money.

To start it off, I just think ultimate freedom is when our cost to survive is very minimal. We have more time to live our lives because we don't have to work so much to cover cost of living and more of our money will go towards what we want. Plus few societies have collapsed because their populous was too educated with their needs met.

I admit it's an in theory pipe dream that's heavily dependent on the population. But when needs are met. The government doesn't need to step into the private sector to protect us from unemployment or under paid.

Welfare is a massive part of the budget because it's covering private costs on their behalf. It's not very sustainable and when automation is coming anyway, we should start with needs.

True. When automation reaches its full potential the biggest limiting agent will be natural resources and intelligent. humans. Like intelligent people that can make new tech and do research that ai can't. The need for menial labor will be gone.
Wants will always become needs over time. For example, the idea of a heart transplant would have been impossibly expensive luxury medicine in my parent's youth.

It was just an expensive need, as they needed it to live. There will always be those as well, but the constant goal should be to get as many alive and educated as we can. With the exception of the violent.

The problem with that is that there's no limit to the amount of resources you can spend on education and healthcare. Imho, government granted rights (if we have to have a government) should be restricted to negative rights.
